promptInstructions: Draft a Special Leave Petition under Article 136. Article 136 is an extraordinary discretionary jurisdiction of the Supreme Court — 'In its discretion, grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order in any cause or matter passed or made by any court or tribunal in the territory of India.'
FORMAT STRICTLY per Supreme Court Rules 2013 Order XXII (civil SLP) / Order XXI (criminal SLP). Filing only through Advocate-on-Record (Order IV).
Cause-title: 'IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA' + jurisdiction line + 'Arising out of the final judgment and order dated ... passed by HC ...'.

Limitation: 90 days from the date of impugned judgment of HC (Article 133 Limitation Act 1963). If review filed in HC, 60 days from review dismissal. Section 5 Limitation Act 1963 for condonation of delay.

Para A: Questions of Law — numbered substantial questions of law of GENERAL public importance. Cite Pritam Singh v. State AIR 1950 SC 169 — Art. 136 'a very wide and discretionary' power exercised sparingly only on exceptional and special circumstances + grave injustice.

Cite N. Suriyakala v. A. Mohan Doss (2007) 9 SCC 196 — discretion of SC; Mathai @ Joby v. George (2016) 7 SCC 700 — Article 136 not regular appeal; Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala (2000) 6 SCC 359 (merger doctrine — once SC dismisses by speaking order, the HC order merges).
Cite Sir Chunilal V. Mehta v. Century Spinning AIR 1962 SC 1314 — substantial question of law definition.

Para B: Declaration — (i) no similar SLP filed; (ii) limitation complied or delay condonation sought; (iii) no review pending in HC (or if filed/dismissed, give details); (iv) all material facts disclosed.
Para C: Limitation — calculate carefully; period excluded for obtaining certified copy.
Para D-F: Statement of facts — brief, material only.
Para G: History of proceedings — Trial Court (judgment + outcome), First Appeal / Revision (judgment + outcome), HC (judgment + outcome). Append all judgments as annexures.
Para H: Grounds — typical grounds:
- HC failed to appreciate substantial question of law of general importance
- HC perversely reversed concurrent findings without justification
- HC failed to consider material evidence
- HC misapplied / misread precedent
- Grave miscarriage of justice — shocks conscience of court
- In criminal SLP: HC failed to consider Section 313 statement; appreciation of evidence perverse; sentence shockingly disproportionate.
Cite criminal SLP grounds — Hari Singh v. Sukhbir Singh (1988) 4 SCC 551; Smt. Dalbir Kaur v. State of Punjab (1976) 4 SCC 158; Arunachalam v. PSR Sadhanantham (1979) 2 SCC 297.
Para I: Interim relief — stay of impugned order; status quo pending hearing.
Para J: Where review petition dismissed by HC, attach review judgment + impugned judgment.
Order of papers per SC Rules Order XXII Rule 2 — cover page; list of dates; questions of law; declarations; SLP body; annexures (HC judgment first); affidavit; AOR vakalatnama.
AOR alone files. AOR certificate signed.
Court fee — Schedule II SC Rules; civil SLP higher than criminal.
Caveat: Where impugned order is interlocutory, very rare leave. Where review by SC against own order, separate procedure (curative).
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Special leave to appeal — discretionary jurisdiction of SC
Power to do complete justice — ancillary to SLP
90 days for SLP from HC judgment
Exclusion of period for certified copy

filing_checklist: SLP paperbook per SC Rules 2013 Order XXII — original + 5 copies (typed/printed)
Annexures — impugned HC order (P-1), trial court judgment, lower appellate judgment, pleadings
Application for condonation of delay (if applicable) with separate affidavit
Court fee per Schedule II SC Rules
Certified copy of impugned HC order
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: respondents_list must not be empty (include State in criminal SLP)
impugned_order_date must not be in future
limitation_calculation must not be empty — flag if days elapsed > 90 (or > 60 from review dismissal)
If delay > 0, delay_in_filing must include reasons
advocate_on_record must not be empty (AOR mandatory)
Court level restricted to Supreme Court only
